title: Hotpath kernel handoff and layer-prefetch orchestrator for paged-attention KV management
creator: Arjun Patel
description: Goal: implement a hotpath-aware kernel selection and a layer-prefetch orchestration layer for paged-attention KV caches. The feature combines (1) per-layer microbenchmarking and a microkernel fallback table that allows runtime switching between fused/unfused attention kernels and quantized execution paths, and (2) an entropy-driven prefill priority and 'shadow-reservoir' eviction/compaction system to reduce fragmentation and tail latency for long-context workloads. This ticket covers design, prototype, perf validation, and a small rollout to dedicated pools.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime selects optimal kernel variant per request/sequence length with <2% error vs offline oracle
End-to-end median latency improvement of >=5% and 95th percentile tail latency reduction >=8% on our long-context benchmark suite compared to baseline
Token cost (in GPU time) reduced or equal for at least 90% of queries on the production traffic sample
Eviction system limits inter-shard fragmentation growth to <10% over 24h in synthetic long-session tests
Automated fallback to conservative conservative-kernel + decode-slow-path on OOMs with no request loss
Design doc and rollout plan approved by Runtime and Platform leads; required PRs merged and demo in Canary cluster

perf_summary: Early prototype (dev cluster) shows median decode latency down 6%-9% across long-context testrun (ctx=32k tokens) and 95th tail improved 9%-12% when hotpath selection used with layer-prefetch. Token GPU time reduced ~3% overall; savings concentrated on requests with frequent layer reuse. Microbenchmark startup adds ~4ms per model load but amortized over session lifetime.
risks_mitigations: Risk: kernel switching increases codepath complexity and may regress cold-starts. Mitigation: keep microkernel table load optional behind flag; validate with canary and keep conservative default.
Risk: prefetching could increase memory pressure. Mitigation: entropy-driven scoring + adaptive concurrency cap to stop prefetching when free memory < threshold.
Risk: background compaction could cause transient stalls. Mitigation: compactor runs at low-priority IO/CPU quotas and uses time-slicing; emergency abort on scheduler pressure.

implementation_notes: Per-layer perf probes are executed once per model load plus periodic jittered re-checks to adapt to thermal/perf drift.
Kernel-table format: (layer_id -> sorted list of kernel candidates with score, fallback flag, estimated mem footprint). Table serialized in model metadata and hot-swappable during runtime upgrades.
Prefetch priority uses a composite score: token_entropy * recency_weight * reuse_predictor (small ML model). We keep the reuse_predictor cheap (logistic regression) to avoid compute overhead.
Shadow-reservoir compactor: maintains a small hot-reservoir per shard where pages are coalesced in-place during low-load windows; cold pages eligible for probabilistic eviction.
Monitoring: emit 'kernel_selected', 'prefetch_issued', 'compaction_run' events with shard/layer tags; add SLO alerts for +3% regressions in token GPU time.
